speaker: dad
igboText: Nwa nwa m nwanyị, ka m kọọrọ gị akụkọ gbasara Mbe na Nduru.
englishText: My granddaughter, let me tell you a story about Tortoise and Dove.
statement: Dad tells his granddaughter a story about Tortoise and Dove.
falseStatement: Dad tells his grandson a story about Tortoise and Dove.

speaker: granddaughter
statement: The granddaughter asks if they were friends.
falseStatement: The granddaughter asks if they were enemies.

speaker: dad
igboText: Ee. Ha biri ọnụ ma rie ọnụ.
englishText: Yes. They lived together and ate together.
statement: Dad says they lived together and ate together.
falseStatement: Dad says they lived apart and ate together.

speaker: granddaughter
falseStatement: The granddaughter asks where it happened.

speaker: dad
igboText: Otu ụbọchị, Mbe tinyere iwu. "Ị ga-ekwu aha gị tupu i rie nri."
englishText: One day, Tortoise made a law. "You must say your name before you eat."
statement: Dad says Tortoise made a rule that each person must say their name before eating.
falseStatement: Dad says Tortoise made a rule that you must eat before saying your name.

speaker: granddaughter
statement: The granddaughter says the rule sounds easy.
falseStatement: The granddaughter says the rule sounds hard.

speaker: dad
igboText: Ọ bụghị mfe maka Nduru. Ọ na-asụ nsụ.
statement: Dad says it was not easy for Dove because he stammered.
falseStatement: Dad says it was easy for Dove because he spoke clearly.

speaker: dove
statement: Dove stammers while trying to say his name.

speaker: dad
igboText: Ka Nduru na-agbalị, Mbe tiri mkpu, "Mbe!" wee rie pap niile.
englishText: While Dove struggled, Tortoise shouted, "Tortoise!" and ate all the porridge.
statement: Dad says Tortoise shouted his own name and ate all the porridge while Dove struggled.
falseStatement: Dad says Tortoise shouted "Dove!" and ate all the porridge while Dove struggled.

speaker: granddaughter
statement: The granddaughter says that was unfair.
falseStatement: The granddaughter says that was fair.

speaker: dad
igboText: N'ụbọchị ọzọ, Nduru tinyere iwu. "Ị ga-asa aka gị ma debe ha ọcha tupu i rie nri."
englishText: The next day, Dove made a law. "You must wash your hands and keep them clean before you eat."
statement: Dad says Dove made a new rule to wash and keep hands clean before eating.
falseStatement: Dad says Dove made a new rule to eat before washing hands.

speaker: granddaughter
statement: The granddaughter asks what happened next.
falseStatement: The granddaughter asks who made the next rule.

speaker: dad
igboText: Nduru sachara aka ya wee fee n'ofe.
englishText: Dove washed his hands and flew to the soup.
statement: Dad says Dove washed his hands and flew to the soup.
falseStatement: Dad says Dove flew to the soup without washing his hands.

speaker: dad
igboText: Ọ sachara aka ya, ma oge ọ bụla ọ na-arị arị, ha na-emerụkwa ọzọ.
englishText: He washed his hands, but every time he crawled, they got dirty again.
statement: Dad says Tortoise kept getting his hands dirty again while crawling.
falseStatement: Dad says Tortoise kept his hands clean while crawling.

speaker: granddaughter
igboText: Ya bụ o nweghị ike iri nri?
statement: The granddaughter asks if Tortoise could not eat.
falseStatement: The granddaughter asks if Tortoise could eat quickly.

speaker: dad
igboText: Nke ahụ bụ eziokwu. Nduru riri ofe niile.
englishText: That's right. Dove ate all the soup.
statement: Dad says Dove ate all the soup.
falseStatement: Dad says Tortoise ate all the soup.

speaker: granddaughter
igboText: Mgbe ahụ gịnị ka ha mụtara?
statement: The granddaughter asks what they learned.
falseStatement: The granddaughter asks why they made more rules.

speaker: dad
igboText: Ha mụtara na iwu ịchọ onwe onye na-emerụ onye ọ bụla. Site n'oge ahụ, ha kwụsịrị ime iwu ịchọ onwe onye ma biri n'udo.
englishText: They learned that selfish rules hurt everyone. After that, they stopped making selfish laws and lived in peace.
statement: Dad says they learned selfish rules hurt everyone and then chose to live in peace.
falseStatement: Dad says they learned selfish rules help everyone and then fought more.
